about: The golden fixture volume set for the clean-room rewrite (issue #5, section 6.1). One volume per shape the format can take, so a baseline that passes across this set has been through every structural case the reader can meet. Each entry names the exact bundle file the registry serves for that slug -- the newest-wins fold picks it out of the many builds installed -- pinned by its manifest stamp and by the sha256 of the file itself. Classifications were verified by reading the manifests and world payloads out of the zips, not by reputation.
goldenTree: the current tree at branch m0/parity

volumes.title: TUNIC
volumes.why: One world, one lens, one source. The baseline shape a MapGenie game arrives in: nothing merged, nothing split, nothing sharded, every collection a point collection drawn as pins.

volumes.title: Cyberpunk 2077
volumes.why: Two sources in one world. The merge ledger names Piggyback as the origin and IGN Wiki as a donor that matched 270 locations and added 37 of its own (alignment: 99 anchors, median 26.0px, p90 52.0px, worst 67.4px); the donor also arrives as a second lens over the same ground. Verified by reading worlds/night-city.json out of the zip -- the candidate was checked rather than assumed, and it does merge.

volumes.title: Fallout: New Vegas
volumes.why: Thirteen worlds, eight of them pieces cut from the Mojave sheet and carrying it as their parent. The split is the case where several places share one tile pyramid and the composer takes the sheet apart rather than showing it whole.

volumes.title: Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
volumes.why: The only installed volume whose lenses carry distinct shard ids -- Sky 1783, Surface 1784, Depths 1785 -- so a location belongs to one lens and switching lenses changes which features exist rather than only which raster is drawn. The suggested candidates (ghost-of-tsushima, sonic-frontiers, marathon) were inspected and all carry shard 0 on every lens; they are multi-world or multi-lens, not sharded.

volumes.title: Mars
volumes.why: The Trek planet: the only surface the viewer offers a globe for. It declares atlas.geometry.surface=sphere with an equirectangular mapping the viewer can invert, carries two lenses over the same ground, and declares a cell grid. Every globe-pane step in the tour is reachable only here.

pendingSlots.wanted: One public city volume: a basemap lens under the national hydrography enrichment, carrying all three geometries at once and a curated atlas.label.policy. It is the only fixture that exercises the path and area legend and the label-policy ladder end to end.
pendingSlots.note: A city volume filling this slot exists on this machine but may not be named in the repository, so it is described in the ignored FIXTURES.private.json and its baseline is written to the ignored golden/parity/private/. The public proof city bend-or takes the slot over as soon as it has a bundle; landing it changes the fixture library from five volumes to six, which moves library.volumes and the game-second target in every baseline, so it is a full re-capture rather than an addition.

notChosen.finding: Two lenses, both shard 0, plus a MapGenie/IGN merge. A second merged volume, not a sharded one.
Four independent worlds, one lens each, all shard 0. Multi-world, not sharded and not split -- no world carries a parent.
